title: The Dragon Within and the Hardened Heart
english: The face which he put on—who is able to expose it? Who is able to uncover it and show what the dragon is within? And a little further on: I ran back in memory to the sacred writings that lie in this divinely inspired book of Job, and as in a bodily shaping, [the sentence is corrupt and has no main verb; roughly:] the exceedingly formless and varied thing hidden among his thoughts and in the stripping away of outward masks, describing the devil and the demons, the source of evil and of wicked things. For he says, “Who will uncover the face of his covering?” (Job 41:5 (41:13)).

And since there was a contention over this outward, visible variety, as they rise up from some depth of unseen vice, these words are also added to what has been said: “Who will uncover the face of his covering?”—that is, who is able to enter into the thoughts of his heart, since they are folded together? “His heart will not be shaken; it is fixed like a stone, and it stands like an anvil that cannot be hammered” (Job 41:15-16 (41:23-24)). His heart, he says, has turned to stone, and it cannot be beaten out; he is wholly hardened and brazen—not driven, not following reason, not yielding. He is hard, unmalleable, unyielding. And if anyone has drawn power from the devil, he too has the heart of this dragon, unmalleable and not to be driven. But if anyone is gold, following the word, he yields to the goldsmith’s art until he becomes a golden leaf and receives the impressions of the letters of God, in Christ Jesus, to whom be glory to the ages of ages. Amen.

title: Double Blessings After Suffering
english: The text states that affliction required children to be doubled. Observe the livestock: sheep numbered thirty thousand, having begun with seven thousand. Camels totaled six thousand, starting with three thousand. Oxen yokes reached a thousand, initially five hundred. The same pattern applied to donkeys. Sons and daughters born to him totaled ten, matching his previous count. Fourteen children were necessary, along with six, to equal the number of lost offspring. We conclude that sheep and cattle were lost, while sons and daughters died but were not lost. Thus, God granted him an equal number of new children, ensuring double in the resurrection. This made him a father of double the children he once had. If souls perished with death and resurrection were false, fourteen sons and six daughters would have been required. The sacred text preserves the account of him receiving seven sons. If he later had fourteen sons and six daughters while discussing resurrection, the children would be tripled rather than doubled, contradicting their original number.

Job lived one hundred seventy years after the affliction, with his total lifespan reaching two hundred forty. How does this align with his entire life span? Precisely: having received double blessings, even the years of former prosperity are counted doubly. He lived one hundred twenty years in prosperity, then one hundred forty in suffering. The period 'after the affliction' refers not to when it ended but when it began. Following four and ten years of illness, the duration of his suffering is noted.

title: Duration of Job's Life and Resurrection
english: He lived for another [numbers] years. For the [numbers] years of the previous prosperity that occurred, the double duration of the later good deeds [numbers] years accumulates. Including also the [numbers] years of the plague, [numbers] years are added, so that after the plague, he lived [numbers] years as recorded. Thus, the double repayment of his prosperity is preserved. Therefore, calculate as follows: he lived in wealth and good upbringing for [numbers] years. In the total decline and the body's affliction, [numbers] years. In the second period of good deeds, [numbers] years, making the total span of his life [numbers] years, as the sacred book states.

Job died aged and full of days. It is written that he will be raised with those whom the Lord raises. Akylas and Symmachus, having come together, read the book, following the Hebrew text. Theodotio concludes the [numbers], nothing missing—neither time nor life. It is also written that he will be raised with those whom the Lord raises, clearly the righteous. For the wicked, he says, will not be raised in judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous. We accept these words, even if not as the entire fabric of the text, but as something woven by the holy ones into the book. Nevertheless, we accept all, having received the book from the fathers.

This is interpreted from the Syriac book. Syriac is now the Hebrew dialect, since Syria is called Judean, and many Palestinians refer to Syriacs as such. Herodotus the historian notes: Indoi, Egyptians, Arabs, and Syriacs in Palestine are circumcised. They call the Jews thus.
